correctness.rationale: The focal primary paper proves existence of radii \(r_\varepsilon\) for which \(r_\varepsilon\ge\eta_\varepsilon/K\) and \(\eta_\varepsilon/K\le F_{p,K}(r_\varepsilon)\). Compactness along \(\varepsilon\to0\) gives \(r\ge a=2^{1/p}/K\) and \(a\le F(r)\). Direct differentiation of \(F=u-K^{-1}v\) gives \(F\prime=-A+K^{-1}B\), where \(B/A\le1+((1-r)/r)^{p-1}\). For \(r\ge a\), \(t=K/2^{1/p}-1\), hence \((1-r)/r\le t\). If \(t\le1\) then \(1+t^{p-1}\le2\le K\); otherwise \(1+t^{p-1}\le1+t=K/2^{1/p}<K\) since \(p-1\le1\). This proves \(F\prime\le0\) and hence the new endpoint condition. Strict pointwise improvement over the focal source follows from \((1-a)^p>0\). Independently evaluated the new scalar boundary versus the source simplification: at \(p=1.1\), approximately 4.64478 versus 4.09924, and at \(p=1.5\), approximately 3.40210 versus 3.13728. Values are illustrations; analytic monotonicity is the proof.
correctness.risk: The argument relies on the focal source's intermediate radius estimates; it does not independently rederive its topological witness. The threshold is nontrivially stronger only on a subrange of 1<p<=2, not claimed optimal.

final_claim: For real \(\ell_p\), \(1<p\le2\), any Lipschitz retraction from its closed unit ball to the unit sphere with Lipschitz constant \(K\ge3\) satisfies \(a\le(1-a^p)^{1/p}-K^{-1}(1-a^p+(1-a)^p)^{1/p}\) with \(a=2^{1/p}/K\); this sharpens the focal source's discarded-radical necessary condition on the range where the threshold improves.
limitations: Necessary scalar lower-bound condition, not the exact best Lipschitz retraction constant.
